headline: The core is pulling away from the periphery: Midtown, the West End and King's Cross are tightening on AI and prime demand, while Docklands vacancy hits a record high.
summary: Midtown has the lowest vacancy in London at 4.3% (Avison Young), and Grade A vacancy is 1.3% in both the West End and the City. The West End commands GBP 190 psf against GBP 95 psf in the City (JLL). King's Cross is consolidating as the AI and tech cluster, with Google's 860,000 sq ft HQ complete and OpenAI pre-letting Jahn Court. In contrast, CoStar reports Docklands Core vacancy at 18.6%, the highest since its records began in 2003, despite recent large lettings at Canary Wharf.
insights: West End: rents at a record GBP 190 psf (JLL), Grade A vacancy at 1.3%; Mayfair and St James's lead growth (Avison Young).
City: GBP 95 psf prime rent, Grade A vacancy at 1.3%, and a large 2026 completion pipeline (~4.85m sq ft, Savills via K2 Space).
Midtown: lowest vacancy in London at 4.3%, down 60bp q/q (Avison Young).
King's Cross: the AI and tech hub, with Google's HQ complete (860,000 sq ft) and OpenAI pre-letting Jahn Court (Avison Young).
Canary Wharf / Docklands: record Docklands Core vacancy of 18.6% (CoStar), even as Avison Young lists Canary Wharf among the rental growth markets. The submarket is polarised.

signals.title: Midtown and King's Cross momentum
signals.rationale: The lowest vacancy plus AI and life-science demand make these the strongest non-core growth locations.

signals.title: Docklands structural vacancy
signals.rationale: Record vacancy implies continued pressure on rents and values for non-prime Docklands assets; repositioning or change of use may be needed.
